dedupe_keys.name: him hydrogen infrastructure cost and routing model

description: HIM is a Python hydrogen infrastructure model from Forschungszentrum Jülich researchers. The repository describes spatial analyses of hydrogen supply-chain architectures at nationwide scale and supplies examples of abstract cost assessment and georeferenced infrastructure design. Users set hydrogen production and demand locations, transport modes, pipeline candidates, costs and a study geography. Outputs are network-design or supply-chain cost comparisons for that configuration. Geographic coverage depends on the input country, and the horizon follows scenario assumptions. MIT-licensed source is public. The README says pipeline optimisation uses Gurobi by default but can use another solver; a solver and spatial inputs are needed for an actual run. A limitation is that least-cost routing depends on uncertain demand and permitting assumptions, and a calculated route is not an approved pipeline. HIM supports hydrogen capacity and transport planning. The catalogue's model-pypsa is a different energy-system model, not a HIM component. No geodata or case was downloaded.
inputs: Transport mode, pipeline and cost assumptions
name: HIM hydrogen infrastructure cost and routing model
